extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community: investigators, applicants, grantees, institutional research administrators, and other stakeholders in NIH-funded research
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH extramural policy, process, and resource updates relevant to grant applicants, awardees, and institutional administrators. It highlights new formats, review-process changes, and initiatives affecting applications and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate research models (New Approach Methodologies - NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: "NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose scientifically sound models that maximize human relevance and translational potential, but prioritize the model(s) that best address the specific research question. Consider NAMs where appropriate, but justify model selection relative to the study aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects application format and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: "Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the PF5-specific application format and key features described in NIH guidance. Be aware that applications may be split into linked awards after peer review and before Just-in-Time (JIT) requests — plan collaborative and budgetary components accordingly and prepare to respond to potential splitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans, use the 2026 Pilot format and include the specified (simplified) required elements. Follow NIH instructions for content and structure of the pilot format to meet policy expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility in applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: "Embedding Replication and Reproducibility Throughout NIH Research: Key Reminders for Applications, Awards, and a New Highlighted Topic. The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science... NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address replication and reproducibility explicitly in applications where relevant (methods, design, statistical considerations, plans for replication). Align proposals with the Gold Standard Science goals and anticipate NIH expectations from the Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to incentivize and institutionalize replication efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding 'Competitive But Not Discussed' (CBND) review designation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should know that being scored below the top one-third can result in a CBND designation — an acknowledgment that an application may be competitive yet not discussed. Understand how this designation may affect next steps, resubmission strategy, and administrative actions following review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized NIH peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR)
rubrics_metrics.description: "In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR)... providing an update on the consolidation and its initial effects on the peer-review process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect NIH peer review processes to be centralized under CSR, with implications for review procedures, timelines, and possibly study section composition. This consolidation is intended to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency — plan application timing and responsiveness to review-related requests with this structure in mind.
